title: O Unexhausted Grace
description: O Unexhausted Grace in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 172.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O un-ex-haust-ed grace! O love un-search-a-ble! I am not gone to my own_ place, I am not yet in hell! Earth doth not o-pen yet, My soul to swal-low up! And hang-ing o'er the burn-ing pit, I still am forced to hope.

lines: I am not gone to my own place,
I am not yet in hell!
And hanging o'er the burning pit,
I still am forced to hope.
I hope at last to find
The settled peace, the constant mind,
That makes me meet for home:
I hope to see thy glorious face,
What shall I do to keep
Still let me pray, and watch, and weep,
Enter with all thy mercy's power,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
